checks.do: Whether extranet, API protection, AppProtection and reauth flags are unchanged after an apply that changed only a name or port range, by re-reading the segment.
Whether every configured server group reached ZPA, since only the IDs in the first `server_groups` block are sent.
Which policy types hold APP operands that name the ID of a destroyed segment.
Whether the remote inspection profile association is set, by reading the profile from the API, since state reflects the configured value.

parent-flags-always-serialized.statement: The SDK request structs for the four application segment kinds declare some API flags without `omitempty`, so they are always in the request body, as false when the caller leaves them unset: `extranetEnabled`, `apiProtectionEnabled`, `autoAppProtectEnabled` and `adpEnabled` on the main segment; `extranetEnabled`, `apiProtectionEnabled` and `bypassOnReauth` on browser access; `extranetEnabled` and `apiProtectionEnabled` on inspection and PRA.

parent-flags-never-set.statement: The four resources build the request from Terraform arguments and never assign the unmodeled flags: the main segment expander sets `APIProtectionEnabled` and `BypassOnReauth` but not `ExtranetEnabled`, `AutoAppProtectEnabled` or `ADPEnabled`; the browser access expander sets none of its three; the inspection and PRA expanders set neither `ExtranetEnabled` nor `APIProtectionEnabled`. The schemas have no matching arguments to read.
parent-flags-never-set.conditions: Absence claim. Searched with `git -C vendor/terraform-provider-zpa grep -n -i -E 'extranetenabled|autoappprotect|adpenabled|apiprotectionenabled|bypassonreauth' <ref> -- zpa/resource_zpa_application_segment.go zpa/resource_zpa_application_segment_browser_access.go zpa/resource_zpa_application_segment_inspection.go zpa/resource_zpa_application_segment_pra.go` at v4.4.10 and HEAD. Hits are limited to the assignments quoted here and to reads from the API response (`resp.BypassOnReauth` and similar). The same files were read at both refs; the provider files are unchanged between them.

main-update-builds-from-state.statement: The main application segment update builds its whole request from Terraform arguments. It reads the existing segment only to detect that it is gone, and ignores any other error from that read, discards the result, and sends the rebuilt struct as the PUT body. The SDK's `Update` sends the struct it is given and merges nothing.

unrelated-update-may-blank-flags.statement: So an update that changes only an unrelated argument sends `false` for flags the Terraform schema cannot express, which can switch off extranet, API protection, auto AppProtection, ADP or bypass-on-reauth behavior that was enabled outside Terraform.
unrelated-update-may-blank-flags.conditions: Depends on how ZPA treats a PUT that carries false for a flag that is currently true (gap api-app-segment-put-semantics), and on the browser access, inspection and PRA updates also being full PUTs of a struct rebuilt from state (browser access, inspection and PRA updates read and confirmed as full PUTs of a rebuilt struct).

upstream.note: Filing 11 (ZPA application segments) of the 2026-08 provider audit.

phantom-shared-microtenant-object.statement: Each of the four request structs holds `SharedMicrotenantDetails` by value with `omitempty`, which Go's JSON encoder does not omit. The provider never assigns it on a write (it only reads `SharedToMicrotenants` from a response), so every create and update carries `sharedMicrotenantDetails` with an empty `sharedFromMicrotenant` object.
phantom-shared-microtenant-object.conditions: Absence claim. Searched with `git -C vendor/terraform-provider-zpa grep -n SharedMicrotenantDetails <ref> -- zpa/resource_zpa_application_segment*.go` at v4.4.10 and HEAD: the only hit is the response read in the main segment resource. The nested `SharedFromMicrotenant` field is also a value struct tagged `omitempty`. What ZPA does with the empty object is gap empty-object-semantics in shared.sdk-go.zero-value-writes.

upstream.note: Filing 11 (ZPA application segments) of the 2026-08 provider audit.

inspection-subapp-flags-always-serialize.statement: The inspection nested-app struct (`AppsConfig`) sends `enabled`, `adpEnabled`, `allowOptions`, `hidden`, `trustUntrustedCert` and `portal` without `omitempty`. The SDK's inspection `Update` only injects `appId` and `inspectAppId` into those entries, matching by name; it does not copy the other fields from the existing app.

evidence.after: func Update(ctx context.Context, service *zscaler.Service, id string, appSegmentInspection *AppSegmentInspection)

inspection-subapp-expand-subset.statement: The inspection resource's expander builds each nested app from a subset of fields (ids, name, description, port, protocol, certificate, domain, trust-untrusted-cert, app types). It does not assign `Enabled`, `AdpEnabled`, `AllowOptions`, `Hidden` or `Portal`, and the `Protocols` assignment is commented out in both the expander and the flattener.
inspection-subapp-expand-subset.conditions: Absence claim for the unassigned fields. Searched the `expandInspectionAppsConfig` body in zpa/resource_zpa_application_segment_inspection.go at v4.4.10 and HEAD (unchanged between them); the struct literal there lists exactly the assigned fields. The commented lines are quoted.

inspection-update-may-reset-subapp-state.statement: So updating an inspection segment sends every nested app with `enabled`, `adpEnabled`, `allowOptions`, `hidden`, `portal` false and no protocol list, whatever those apps hold remotely.
inspection-update-may-reset-subapp-state.conditions: Depends on how ZPA treats those members in a PUT (gap api-app-segment-put-semantics).

browser-hidden-sent-false.statement: The browser access resource has no `hidden` argument. Its expander for clientless apps assigns `AllowOptions`, `Enabled` and others but not `Hidden`, and the SDK declares `Hidden` without `omitempty`, so every clientless app in a create or update carries `hidden: false`.
browser-hidden-sent-false.conditions: Absence claim. Searched `git -C vendor/terraform-provider-zpa grep -n -i hidden <ref> -- zpa/resource_zpa_application_segment_browser_access.go` at v4.4.10 and HEAD: no hits. That the API then un-hides a hidden app is not shown by the client (gap api-app-segment-put-semantics); only the wire value is claimed.

upstream.note: Filing 11 (ZPA application segments) of the 2026-08 provider audit.

pra-update-sends-remote-values.statement: On a PRA segment update, every nested app whose domain already exists remotely is rebuilt from the remote object (name, enabled, port, protocol, connection security, domain, description). The configured values for that app are used only to decide whether its domain is still present. Only apps with a new domain are taken from the configuration. A change to an existing app's port, protocol, connection security, name or description is therefore not sent.

upstream.note: Filing 11 (ZPA application segments) of the 2026-08 provider audit.

browser-child-id-positional-fallback.statement: For a clientless app with an empty ID, the browser access SDK `Update` assigns the ID of the existing app at the same list position. The provider fills IDs by name first, so only apps whose name matches no existing app (new or renamed) reach the positional fallback. Those apps come from a Terraform set, whose list order is not the order of the remote list.

browser-child-id-may-duplicate.statement: So adding or renaming a clientless app can give it the ID of an existing app that another entry in the same request already carries by name, producing a request in which two entries have one ID and one existing app is replaced or overwritten.
browser-child-id-may-duplicate.conditions: Depends on the position the new entry takes in the set's list order, on the new entry's index being below the length of the existing list, and on how ZPA treats two entries with the same ID (gap api-app-segment-put-semantics). Not exercised against a live API.

nested-apps-matched-by-name.statement: The inspection and PRA SDK `Update` functions find each existing nested app through a map keyed by name. Two desired apps with the same name both receive the same ID, and a renamed app is treated as new. The inspection resource sets each nested app's name to its domain, so the identity in practice is the domain.

main-share-separate-write.statement: Sharing a main application segment to microtenants is a second API call made after the segment is written. On create, the ID is set before the share call, and a share failure returns an error with the segment already created. On update, a share failure returns an error after the parent PUT has been applied. Neither path rolls back.

association-block-first-only.statement: The helper that turns the `server_groups` argument into a request reads only the first block (`blocks[0]`) and ignores any others, with no error. Only the IDs inside the first block are sent.

upstream.note: Filing 11 (ZPA application segments) of the 2026-08 provider audit.

association-block-first-only-places.statement: The same first-block-only read is in the other association expanders in `common.go` (app connector groups, app server groups, service edge groups), which feed the v1 and v2 access policy rules, the redirection rule and the server group resource, and in the server group, service edge group (`trusted_networks`) and user portal link expanders, where the schema allows several blocks (the private cloud and `service_edges` expanders are single-block by schema).
association-block-first-only-places.conditions: Search: `git -C vendor/terraform-provider-zpa grep -n 'blocks\[0\]' v4.4.10 -- zpa` lists zpa/common.go (four helpers), resource_zpa_private_cloud.go, resource_zpa_server_group.go, resource_zpa_service_edge_group.go (two) and resource_zpa_user_portal_link.go. Callers: `grep -n -E 'expandCommon(AppConnector|ServiceEdge)Groups|expandAppServerGroups'` shows the policy access rule (v1, v2), redirection rule and server group resources. The `server_groups` argument of the main, browser access, inspection and PRA segment resources is read at v4.4.10 as `Type: schema.TypeList, Optional: true` with no `MaxItems` (searched the schema block in each file); a configuration with two blocks therefore plans and applies, and sends the first block's IDs only. Checked: the private cloud summary fields and the service edge group `service_edges` have `MaxItems: 1`, so first-only is by design there; the server group `servers` and `app_connector_groups`, service edge group `trusted_networks` and user portal link `user_portals` schemas have no `MaxItems` (or it is commented out), as do the policy rule and redirection rule association arguments.

main-delete-v1-cleanup-ignores-errors.statement: Deleting a main application segment calls a cleanup that returns nothing. The cleanup lists rules of five policy types through the v1 policy controller, skips a policy type when listing its set or rules fails, skips a rule when its update fails, and the delete then runs regardless.

other-segment-deletes-skip-policy-detach.statement: The browser access, inspection and PRA delete functions do not call the policy cleanup. Browser access calls the SDK delete directly, inspection first removes the segment from its segment group when `segment_group_id` is set, and PRA has a policy-detach call commented out (named for connector groups, not for application segments). All three SDK delete calls pass `ForceDelete: true`.

delete-can-leave-policy-references.statement: So a destroy of a main segment can finish successfully while a policy rule still has an APP operand for it (a cleanup step was skipped or failed), and a destroy of a browser access, inspection or PRA segment does not remove such operands before asking ZPA to delete the segment with force.
delete-can-leave-policy-references.conditions: Depends on ZPA accepting a forced delete of a segment that policy rules reference, and on what it does with those references (gap zpa.terraform.delete-paths:api-delete-referenced-object), and on whether the v1 listing returns rules created through the v2 endpoints, which the main cleanup, unlike the segment group cleanup, does not list separately (gap api-v1-listing-covers-v2-rules). The v1 `UpdateRule` it uses also blanks operand names (zpa.terraform.policy-rule-writes:v1-sdk-erases-operand-names).

associate-all-controls-no-false-branch.statement: The inspection profile resource calls `PutAssociate` only when `associate_all_controls` is true, in both create and update, and never calls the SDK's `PutDeassociate`. Read sets the argument from its own configured value, not from the API. Changing it from true to false therefore sends nothing that de-associates, and state shows false.

api-app-segment-put-semantics.title: How ZPA treats false, empty-object and duplicate-ID members in application segment PUTs
api-app-segment-put-semantics.blocks: saying whether the wire values above clear, keep or reject remote state
api-app-segment-put-semantics.detail: The client sends false for unmodeled flags, hidden false, zeroed nested-app flags, empty association objects, and in one path an ID shared by two entries. No captured source says what ZPA does with each. Test in a scratch tenant: enable a flag outside Terraform, apply an unrelated change, and re-read the segment; repeat with a hidden clientless app and with an inspection nested app that has options enabled.

api-v1-listing-covers-v2-rules.title: Whether the v1 policy listing returns rules written through the v2 endpoints
api-v1-listing-covers-v2-rules.blocks: saying whether the main segment delete cleanup reaches APP operands in rules created through the v2 resources
api-v1-listing-covers-v2-rules.detail: The main cleanup lists rules with the v1 policy controller only. Create a rule with a v2 resource that has an APP operand for a test segment, then list the policy type through the v1 call and check whether the rule and operand appear.
